newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian doctors strike over training changes.
newsitem.headline: Australian doctors strike over training changes.

text.p: About 2,000 Australian junior doctors went on strike on Monday over training changes they believe will leave some doctors unemployed.
The start of the week-long strike in New South Wales, Australia's most populous state, disrupted elective surgery in many hospitals although emergency and children's services remained intact.
At a Sydney rally, junior doctors called for the repeal of legislation stopping newly qualified doctors from working in general practices until they complete a further three years' training.
The legislation limits the distribution of the "Medicare Provider Numbers" which allow doctors to bill their services to the government.
A spokesman for the strikers, Dr Choong-Siew Yong, said doctors believed there would be too few training places, and not enough jobs in the public hospital system to employ all of those who miss out.
"It's really denying people the opportunity to train for their work," said Yong.
Junior doctors also see a plan to link the training to poorly serviced rural areas as "a form of conscription".
But the government said it would not back down.
"We are not going to change our mind on this," Prime Minister John Howard said on Sydney radio.
The legislation would improve training for general practitioners, get more doctors into rural areas, and restrain the growth in the number of general practitioners, he said.
Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge said the government had guaranteed a training post to every doctor who wanted one for the next three years.
Junior doctors in Queensland state also held a stop work meeting and protest meetings were planned for other states later this week.
